subject: URGENT: EastUS2 surge — request for geo-reshuffle + exec bridge and one-time credit
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novus-health.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: oncall@novus-health.com, procurements@novus-health.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate + latency from EastUS2 — affecting production inference

Marissa / Rachel,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xxs and token latency from EastUS2 around 08:50 PDT. Consumer traffic started queuing at our side and inference tail latency jumped to ~3.2s for short prompts (normally ~200-300ms). Error rate for inference requests spiked to ~6.4% and we saw a correlated drop in throughput (QPS down ~25% despite similar incoming traffic).

Attached is a short sample of the server-side 5xx traces and KV cache stats we pulled. This is impacting our checkout flow (prediction calls) across two services; we've routed non-critical traffic to a lower-priority endpoint but core workflows remain degraded.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is an isolated AZ issue or a regional routing problem? Our SRE asked to escalate if cross-region reshuffle is recommended — we may need a geo-steer while you triage. We also need a flag on credits / SLA given the customer impact.

Alice Chen
Operations Lead, Novus Health
(alice.chen@novus-health.com)

Attachments: eastus2-500s-sample.log, kv-cache-stats-20280703.csv

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novus-health.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency from EastUS2 — affecting production inference

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the traces. We're seeing elevated 5xx counts and increased tail latency in our EastUS2 telemetry as well. Initial surface-level checks show higher KV cache eviction churn on a subset of hosts combined with CPU steal on a few GPUs in AZ-a, which would explain the throughput drop and latency tail.

Immediate plan: 
- I'm standing up an internal exec bridge now (details below).
- Ops (internal) will attempt traffic reshuffle (geo-reshuffle) away from EastUS2 to nearby capacity (EastUS1 / EastUS3) for customer-critical routes only. This is a short-term mitigation while we stabilize AZ-a hosts.
- We'll also prepare a one-off credit request for Novus given the impact — draft attached.

Alice, can your SRE confirm whether Novus can accept short-lived geo-steer to EastUS1 for the next 60-90 minutes? We'll only move critical traffic and keep the rest on normal routes.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: credit-request-draft-v1.pdf

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: ACTION: Exec bridge request + approval for geo-reshuffle + provisional credit (Novus Health)

Team — quick brief and ask: Novus Health (HSS-7721) is experiencing a production-impacting surge in EastUS2 (AZ-a) — elevated 5xxs (~6%) and token tail latency causing throughput regression. Customer ops is asking for immediate mitigation; they can tolerate an orchestrated geo-steer for critical routes.

Asks: 
1) Exec bridge now (15 min) to authorize cross-region temporary reshuffle for critical routes and confirm rollback criteria.
2) Approve a one-time provisional credit while we investigate root cause. Suggested band: 20-30% of one-week normal spend for the affected product surface — this is provisional until final billing review.
3) Coordinate billing & support comms (Rachel) and on-call remediation (Soojin & Infra).

Notes: Our mitigation will: perform targeted prefix-level reroutes, enable tighter batching for background workloads, and pin affected customers off AZ-a. We expect reduced customer latency within 10-15 minutes of steering, with full stabilization dependent on replacing/patching the AZ-a hosts.

I am starting the bridge now: Bridge link: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-07-03-eastus2-bridge (ops access).

Marissa

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@novus-health.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 09:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACTION: Exec bridge request + approval for geo-reshuffle + provisional credit (Novus Health)

Marissa / team — approved.

- Exec bridge: go ahead and run the targeted geo-reshuffle for critical prefixes to EastUS1 (limit window to 60 minutes, monitor latency & error rate at 1-minute cadence).
- Provisional credit: approve the provisional band at 25% of one-week spend for the affected inference surface; billing to finalize after post-mortem. Rachel will coordinate with finance and attach an approval ticket.
- Communication: Please use the bridge doc for live notes and add the HubSpot record (HubSpot-987654) to the incident timeline.

Soojin / Vivek — please confirm once the prefix steer is active and share initial latency/error delta. Alice — thanks for coordinating with your oncall; please confirm you received the steer and whether you see expected behavior on your side.

Rachel Kim
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novus-health.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACTION: Exec bridge request + approval for geo-reshuffle + provisional credit (Novus Health)

Quick update from the bridge: 
- 10:03 PDT: started targeted geo-reshuffle of Novus critical prefixes from EastUS2 (AZ-a) -> EastUS1. We limited the change to prediction endpoints only.
- 10:09 PDT: observed immediate drop in 5xx rate from 6.4% -> 0.8% (sampled across service endpoints). Median latency improved from 1.1s -> 250ms; p95 dropped from 2.9s -> 420ms.
- 10:40 PDT: infra team isolated a host-level kernel hang pattern on two AZ-a GPU nodes; those were cordoned and replaced.

Actions completed: 
- Geo-reshuffle active for critical routes.
- Provisional credit approved (Rachel / Billing to ticket).
- Post-mortem owner assigned: OPS-2147 (SRE lead: Vivek).
- Follow-ups: deep KV-cache churn analysis and kernel patch verification (SRE).

Alice — please confirm that from Novus side the checkout flow is back to acceptable levels. We'll keep the geo-reshuffle in place for a hardening window and progressively drain traffic to EastUS2 only after validation. We'll attach the incident artifacts to HubSpot-987654 and the JIRA ticket OPS-2147.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
